topics.topic: How an identical re-upload is identified and whether it invalidates pending import confirmation
questions: How does Registry distinguish the upload for which confirmation was shown from a later upload with identical bytes, and does that later upload invalidate the pending confirmation?
How does Registry distinguish replacement by an identical upload so that the earlier confirmation is invalidated?

Does every accepted re-upload invalidate the pending import confirmation even when the new file has identical bytes and the same digest, and what stored fact or transition distinguishes that replacement?

judgement.why: This is the same question P1 answered, and neither the relevant A13/A16 passages nor the change since closure altered it.

precedent.topic: Whether an identical replacement upload invalidates an existing import confirmation and how replacement is identified
quotes:
The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, in the
   process's memory only — never in the store, never on a disk — until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that
   session — one of the same bytes included — or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.

Confirming a mapping after another file was uploaded in the session is
   refused: the file it named is no longer kept — also when the new file has
   the same bytes.
precedent.why: The texts expressly treat every later upload, identical bytes included, as replacing the earlier file and require the earlier confirmation to be refused; the internal mechanism used to enforce that outcome does not change observable behaviour.
